title: Wren and the Group Chat
premise: Felix Delacroix has spent four years keeping his head down in the small town of Harrow Bend, counting days until graduation frees him. When history teacher Ms. Okafor pairs him with Wren Calloway—the popular girl whose family name is on half the town's buildings—for a semester project on local history, they unearth a decades-old school board cover-up: a student expelled in 1998 for being gay, erased from every record, whose family was quietly destroyed. As Felix and Wren dig deeper, their wary alliance becomes friendship and then something neither expected, forcing Felix to choose between staying invisible until graduation or burning his last semester to force the school board into public reckoning. The book ends at a packed board meeting where Felix testifies, the 1998 expulsion is formally rescinded, and he walks out holding Wren's hand—not fleeing Harrow Bend anymore, but deciding on his own terms whether to stay.
about_author: Zephyrine Voss grew up in a town so small her graduating class fit in one school bus, an experience that taught her both the suffocation and the strange tenderness of small-town life. She writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse to wait politely for permission to exist.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Secret
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He maps his survival strategy for senior year: stay quiet, graduate, leave. A hallway incident—someone scrawling a slur on his locker—reminds him why. Emotional beat: weary resignation disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor announces semester-long local history projects and reads pairings aloud: Delacroix and Calloway. Wren doesn't react; Felix's stomach drops. Emotional beat: dread, the sense that his careful invisibility has been revoked by fiat.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She corners Felix in the library to negotiate: minimal contact, split the work, no drama. Felix agrees too quickly, which annoys her. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion masking mutual curiosity.

chapters.title: Harrow Bend Historical Society, Tuesdays Only
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Their first research trip to a dusty archive run by elderly Mrs. Ibarra yields nothing useful—until Felix finds a gap in the yearbooks: 1998 has no senior superlatives page. Emotional beat: first flicker of shared intrigue.

chapters.title: The Missing Yearbook Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She asks her grandmother about 1998 over dinner and gets a look she can't read—a silence with weight. Her family built this town; she's never questioned what it cost others. Emotional beat: first crack in inherited certainty.

chapters.title: Detention Together
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A librarian misreads their archive bickering as a fight; both get detention. Trapped in a room for two hours, they talk for the first time without armor. Emotional beat: grudging discovery that the enemy is a person.

chapters.title: Danny Reyes
chapters.summary: Mrs. Ibarra, off the record, tells them about Danny Reyes, a senior in 1998 who vanished from records after rumors spread. Expelled, she says, though no paper trail exists. Emotional beat: the project stops being homework and becomes a haunting.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She pulls minutes of 1998 school board meetings through her father's law office connections and finds pages redacted. Her father warns her off: 'Some things are settled.' Emotional beat: loyalty to family versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Group Chat, Population Two
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Wren creates a group chat named 'danny reyes truthers' with just them. Late-night messages turn from research notes to actual conversation. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving sideways, through screens, where it feels safer.

chapters.title: Homecoming, From the Outside
chapters.summary: Felix attends homecoming alone out of obligation, watches Wren laugh with her crowd, leaves early. She notices him go. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by proximity to belonging.

chapters.title: The Best Friend Problem
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her best friend Priya catches Wren laughing at her phone and sees the chat. 'You're actually friends with Felix Delacroix?' The question lands like an accusation. Emotional beat: Wren realizes she's crossed a line she didn't know was drawn.

chapters.title: Records Request, Denied
chapters.summary: Felix files a formal public records request for Danny's disciplinary file. The district denies it within a day—unusually fast. Someone is watching them. Emotional beat: fear replacing curiosity; the stakes become real.

chapters.title: Coach Brandt's Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Coach Brandt, a 1998 grad and current school board ally, pulls Wren aside: 'Whatever you and Delacroix are digging up, drop it. For your own good.' Emotional beat: menace wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Reyes House
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They track down Danny's mother, Marisol, living outside town. She slams the door—then opens it again. 'You're the first person in twenty-five years who asked.' Emotional beat: grief meeting witness.

chapters.title: Marisol's Story
chapters.summary: Marisol recounts it: Danny outed by a note in the locker room, beaten, then expelled for 'conduct unbecoming' while his attackers went unpunished. The family left in shame; Danny later died by suicide. Emotional beat: devastation; Felix sees his own possible past.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Shaken, he almost quits—tells Wren it's not worth it. She argues back, fiercer than he's ever seen her. In the argument, something shifts between them. Emotional beat: conflict as confession; the almost-kiss neither names.

chapters.title: Priya Sides With Nobody
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Priya confronts Wren: help Felix and lose your social standing, or walk away and lose yourself. Priya, unexpectedly, chooses to help—she has her own grievances with the school. Emotional beat: found family beginning to assemble.

chapters.title: The Note in the Locker Room
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. History rhymes: someone leaves a note in Felix's locker echoing 1998's cruelty. But this time three people show up angry on his behalf—Wren, Priya, and quiet Theo from AV club. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into solidarity.

chapters.title: Theo Has Footage
chapters.summary: Theo reveals the security camera above the lockers still works and he archives everything. The vandal is caught on tape: a school board member's nephew. Emotional beat: the powerless discovering they hold leverage.

chapters.title: Thanksgiving Interlude
chapters.summary: Wren invites Felix to her family's chaotic Thanksgiving when she learns he'll be alone. Her grandmother, who went silent about 1998, takes Felix aside: 'I knew Danny. Ask me properly.' Emotional beat: warmth, and a door opening.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Grandmother Calloway admits she was on the student council that voted to stay silent in 1998, pressured by the board. She kept Danny's letters all these years. Emotional beat: guilt across generations, and the gift of evidence.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Danny's letters describe the expulsion, name the board members involved—one of whom still sits on the board today: Richard Hale. Emotional beat: righteous fury; the past is not past.

chapters.title: Richard Hale's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes her father's firm represents Hale. Confronting him, she learns he's known about the cover-up for years—it's why he warned her off. Emotional beat: betrayal inside her own house.

chapters.title: Running Away Is a Plan
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Early acceptance letter arrives from a college far away. Escape is real now. Wren asks if he'd still testify; he can't answer. Emotional beat: love against duty—his duty to himself versus the town.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Wren and Felix fight badly: she accuses him of wanting to be saved rather than to save anyone; he accuses her of playing hero with other people's lives because hers is cushioned. Both are partly right. Emotional beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Silence in the Group Chat
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A week of no messages. Each drafts texts they don't send. Priya referees via separate channels. Emotional beat: the ache of absence proving what presence meant.

chapters.title: Marisol Asks a Question
chapters.summary: Marisol calls Felix: 'Are you doing this for Danny, or for you? Because Danny's gone either way.' Felix finally understands the project was always about the next kid. Emotional beat: clarity through grief.

chapters.title: Apology, Unscripted
chapters.summary: Felix shows up at Wren's window—not romantic, desperate. He apologizes for the parts that were true. She apologizes for hers. They rebuild, honestly this time. Emotional beat: repair; love chosen knowingly.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: The group plans: present everything at the final school board meeting before graduation—letters, footage, testimony. Theo builds a digital archive; Priya handles outreach; Wren will speak despite her father. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing into strategy.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Someone tips off the board. Hale offers Wren a deal: her father's firm gets a prestigious partnership if the archive disappears. She records the offer. Emotional beat: temptation met with cold clarity.

chapters.title: Threats
chapters.summary: Felix's car is keyed; Marisol's door gets egged; Ms. Okafor is quietly reassigned off their project. The machinery of the town pushes back. Emotional beat: fear, but this time they're afraid together.

chapters.title: Ms. Okafor's Desk
chapters.summary: Okafor, packing up her classroom, gives Felix a folder she's kept since 1998—she was Danny's classmate. 'I stayed silent once. Don't be me.' Emotional beat: mentorship as amends; the torch passed.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The group gathers at Wren's house printing documents, rehearsing testimony. Felix and Wren sit on the porch; he tells her he's deferring college. She tells him she applied there too. Emotional beat: quiet joy under pressure; the almost-kiss completed.

chapters.title: Board Meeting, Part One
chapters.summary: The gymnasium is packed—students, Marisol, townsfolk, local press Theo tipped off. Hale tries to gavel through old business first. Priya's organized seating blocks the exits to apathy. Emotional beat: tension coiling toward detonation.

chapters.title: Board Meeting, Part Two: Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix testifies, reading Danny's letters aloud, voice breaking and steadying. Then Marisol stands. Then Grandmother Calloway, stunning the room. Emotional beat: catharsis; private grief made public record.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Wren plays the recording of Hale's bribe offer. The room erupts. Hale resigns on the spot; the board, cornered by press and public, votes unanimously to rescind the 1998 expulsion and issue a formal apology. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, won by witnesses.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The town doesn't transform overnight—some doors stay closed—but the high school installs a scholarship in Danny Reyes's name. Felix walks the halls differently now. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned peace.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At graduation, Ms. Okafor hands diplomas; Felix's name gets the loudest cheer. Wren's father, estranged but present, nods from the back row. Emotional beat: completion; the sentence served turns out to have been commuted.

chapters.title: Deciding to Stay (For Now)
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Felix's POV. College deferred, summer stretching ahead, Felix and Wren drive to the reservoir with Priya and Theo. He could leave. Instead he stays—because leaving would be running, and he's done running. Emotional beat: found family, chosen home, open horizon.
